claim_text: Three previously 'charged' defendants (two undocketed/22-CR-222-adjacent, none previously resolved in this corpus) have dispositions per Sahan Journal's own trackers: Hibo Daar (Hibo Salah Daar), the 71st defendant, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud, admitting she ran Northside Wellness Center Corporation (claimed to serve 40,000 meals weekly, received $2.4 million) and paid $72,000 in bribes to a Feeding Our Future employee, with no sentencing date found; Ahmed Yasin Ali pleaded guilty to one felony count of evading currency reporting obligations, admitting he withdrew $10,000 knowing the funds were proceeds of unlawful activity via a Lake Street Kitchen food site in the JigJiga Business Center, and was sentenced to one year of probation on August 4, 2026, with $61,000 in restitution; Khadar Jigre Adan pleaded guilty in September 2025 to one count of theft of government property (a misdemeanor), admitting he allowed a fraudulent food site to operate out of his JigJiga Business Center for $1,000, and was sentenced to one year of probation on April 29, 2026.

supporting_passages.quote: Ahmed Yasin Ali was sentenced to one year of probation on Aug. 4, 2026... He will pay $61,000 in restitution.
Khadar Adan, 62, was sentenced to one year of probation on April 29, 2026. He pleaded guilty to one count of theft of government property, a misdemeanor, in September 2025.
Hibo Salah Daar, 51, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud. She ran Northside Wellness Center Corporation... admitted to paying $72,000 in bribes to a Feeding Our Future employee.

amounts.methodology: Ahmed Yasin Ali's restitution as ordered at sentencing, per Sahan Journal; not yet confirmed against a primary judgment.
Khadar Jigre Adan's restitution, per Sahan Journal; the $1,000 he was paid to allow a fraudulent food site to use his business address.

qualifiers: No primary court record has been captured for any of the three; all dispositions rest on Sahan Journal's own reporting.

Khadar Jigre Adan's offense (misdemeanor theft of government property) and penalty (probation) are markedly less severe than most other FOF defendants; this reflects his comparatively minor role (allowing use of his business address) rather than direct participation in inflating meal counts.

Ahmed Yasin Ali's offense (evading currency reporting obligations) is likewise a narrower charge than wire fraud or money laundering; treat this as a distinct disposition from the broader fraud allegations, not a resolution of the full scheme allegation against him.
editorial_notes: Part of the defendant-by-defendant disposition reconciliation pass following the 'we need to cover all' instruction.
